questions.question: What is the most common cause of hypothyroidism?
questions.detail: Hashimoto thyroiditis is identified as the most frequent cause of hypothyroidism.

questions.question: Hashimoto thyroiditis is an autoimmune condition triggered by autoantibodies against which of the following?
questions.detail: The disease is caused by autoantibodies that target thyroglobulins.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic ultrasound finding of Hashimoto thyroiditis?
choices: A single, large, solid hypervascular nodule
Thickened isthmus and a micronodular/coarsened gland
questions.detail: Ultrasound typically reveals a thickened isthmus and a gland with a coarsened or micronodular texture.

questions.question: Patients diagnosed with Hashimoto thyroiditis have an increased risk of developing which specific malignancy?
questions.detail: There is a recognized increased risk for thyroid lymphoma in patients with this condition.

questions.question: Which subtype of thyroid cancer is considered very rare but associated with the worst clinical prognosis?
questions.detail: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is rare but carries the most unfavorable prognosis.

questions.question: How many parathyroid glands do the majority of patients typically possess?
questions.detail: Most patients have four parathyroid glands.

questions.question: What is the most frequent clinical indication for parathyroid imaging?
choices: Workup of hypercalcemia for suspected adenoma or hyperplasia
Staging of thyroid squamous cell carcinoma
questions.detail: Imaging is most often performed during the workup of hypercalcemia to evaluate for parathyroid adenoma or hyperplasia.

questions.question: Which syndrome is characteristically linked to the development of parathyroid adenomas or hyperplasia?
questions.detail: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type I (MEN I) is associated with parathyroid abnormalities.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized ectopic location for a parathyroid gland?
questions.detail: Ectopic parathyroid glands can be found in the upper mediastinum, tracheoesophageal groove, and thoracic inlet, but the internal auditory canal is not a recognized site.

questions.question: Parathyroid localization imaging is most frequently indicated in which of the following clinical settings?
choices: In the re-operative setting for persistent or recurrent disease
Only if the patient is pregnant
To distinguish between adenoma and carcinoma
Only in patients with MEN II
questions.detail: Localization studies are most commonly indicated when a patient requires re-operation for persistent or recurrent parathyroid disease.

questions.question: Is it generally considered easy to distinguish between a parathyroid adenoma and a parathyroid carcinoma on imaging studies?
questions.detail: Distinguishing between a parathyroid adenoma and a carcinoma using imaging is rare or difficult.

questions.question: In its end-stage, Hashimoto thyroiditis may manifest as which type of gland on imaging?
questions.detail: While it may initially be enlarged, end-stage Hashimoto thyroiditis often results in an atrophic gland.

questions.question: Graves disease typically presents with which characteristic ultrasound finding?
questions.detail: Graves disease characteristically displays diffuse hypervascularity, often referred to as a 'thyroid inferno'.

questions.question: Anatomically, parathyroid glands are usually found in what relationship to the thyroid gland?
questions.detail: The parathyroid glands are typically located adjacent to the thyroid gland.

questions.question: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma of the thyroid typically presents on imaging as which of the following?
questions.detail: The typical imaging presentation for thyroid Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a solid nodule.
